observations: A deep brown-black field holds a central figure outlined in thick pink, with two rectangular grid-filled openings at the bottom containing white interior shapes that suggest teeth rows behind a barred or grated enclosure.
Two red circles, each crossed by a lime-green X, appear at upper-left and mid-right, offset rather than symmetrically placed, anchoring those zones with a repeating pattern.
Multicolor spiral forms occupy the upper-right and lower-left corners, while a yellow zigzag shape rises from the top-center of the figure above a blue-and-brown face area.
reading: A black ground pushes a pink-outlined figure forward, its lower half split into two grid-filled arches with visible white tooth-like rows. The paired red-and-lime X circles create a visual rhythm that reads more like a system than decoration. Spiral corners pull outward while the central form holds its ground, producing a tension between containment and expansion that sits somewhere between alarm and ceremony.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors #6 and #8. Where #6 scatters figures across a dark purple field, #7 consolidates mass into one dominant pink-outlined form against near-black, making the X-circle motif more prominent.

connections.reason: Both works use the crossed-circle motif and white-outlined figures on a dark ground, but #6 scatters multiple figures across a purple field while #7 compresses everything into one frontal form against near-black.

rawblocks #59 also builds a large frontal figure with circular eye forms and a tooth-row mouth, but against a flat blue field rather than near-black, making the structural parallel visible while the color mood differs sharply.

lookingQuestion: The two red-and-lime X circles sit at upper-left and mid-right rather than at matching positions — how does their off-axis placement affect how you read the central figure?
ambiguities: The yellow zigzag at top-center could be read as a crown, a collar, or an independent form; no supplied evidence resolves which reading the work supports.
nnotb #8 was inspected but its muted earth-tone field and scattered animal-like silhouettes share no strong formal element with #7's X-circle system, so it was omitted as a weak match.
